# Wiring skills into CLAUDE.md

A skill that never loads is dead weight. CLAUDE.md is always in context, so it is where routing and
the staleness rule belong.

## The marker convention

Everything this skill generates lives between markers so later runs regenerate it without touching
hand-written content:

```
<!-- BEGIN skills-map — generated by project-skills-map. Edit rows freely; keep the markers. -->
...generated block...
<!-- END skills-map -->
```

Rules:

- **Never** edit outside the markers without asking.
- If markers exist, replace what is between them and keep surrounding text byte-identical.
- If they do not exist, insert the block **high up** — right after the project's opening description,
  before Repo Structure. Routing that appears after 200 lines of stack detail gets skipped.
- If CLAUDE.md already has a hand-written skills table, fold its rows into the generated one and show
  the user the diff rather than silently dropping their wording.
- No CLAUDE.md at all? Create a minimal one: title, one-line description, then the block.

## The block

Fill in one row per skill. Keep the left column in the vocabulary the person writing the prompt would
use — paths *and* task words, because matching happens on either.

````markdown
<!-- BEGIN skills-map — generated by project-skills-map. Edit rows freely; keep the markers. -->

## Context Loading

Do NOT start a task by exploring with Read/Grep. The conventions live in **skills** — load the
matching skill with the Skill tool as soon as you know which files the task touches. Each one carries
the patterns, the file map, and the gotchas, so no rediscovery is needed.

| Files / task                                                      | Skill                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `apps/server/{routes,services,repositories}/` — endpoints, logic  | `server-api-endpoint`      |
| `apps/server/{models,migrations}/` — schema, DDL                  | `server-models-migrations` |
| DB row/data changes — seed, backfill, one-off fix                 | `db-data-scripts`          |
| `apps/web/api/` — React Query hooks, calling the backend          | `web-data-layer`           |
| `apps/web/app/` — pages, routing, navigation                      | `web-page`                 |
| Role access, menu visibility, permission grants                   | `role-based-access`        |

### Keeping skills current

When a change alters **how a domain works** — not just adding another instance of an existing
pattern — the covering skill is now wrong. Say so and offer to fix it:

> "This changed the mutation contract that `web-data-layer` documents. Want me to refresh that skill?"

Treat these as triggers: a new layer or file role; a changed contract, envelope, or signature; a
replaced library; a new rule others must follow; a convention deliberately broken. Adding one more
route that follows the existing pattern is **not** a trigger.

Run `/project-skills-map` to refresh — it diffs against `.claude/skills-map.json` and only touches
what moved. Also run it when a new module or app lands, since nothing covers it yet.

<!-- END skills-map -->
````

## Why the rule is phrased that way

The failure mode is not "Claude forgets to mention it" — it is mentioning it on **every** change,
which trains the user to ignore the prompt. The convention/instance distinction is the whole point:
it fires on the change that invalidates documentation and stays quiet for routine additions. Keep the
worked example sentence; a concrete phrasing gets imitated far more reliably than an abstract rule.

## Row quality

Left column should read like something a person would say or a path they would open.

Good: `` `apps/web/app/` — pages, routing, navigation ``
Weak: `` Frontend stuff `` (matches nothing specific)
Weak: `` apps/web/app `` (path only — misses "add a page for X")

Keep rows in the same order as the repo structure section, so the two read together.

## Placement in a monorepo

Skills at `.claude/skills/` and one table in the root CLAUDE.md is right for most repos.

For a repo of genuinely independent sub-projects, directory-scoped skills
(`apps/web/.claude/skills/`) only load in that tree. If you use them, still list them in the root
table with their scope marked, or nobody discovers they exist.

## Adjacent docs

Skills should point at living inventories rather than duplicating them — a route list or page index
goes stale inside a skill but stays fresh in a doc that gets updated with each addition. If the repo
has such docs, add a second small table beneath the skills table, and make each skill say "update
this doc when you add one."
